name: China economy
summary: Regulators pause IPOs to steady falling stocks; factory PMI in contraction
state: Chinese regulators told banks to pause IPOs and large share sales to steady a falling stock market, the FT reported on 3 Nov (via Yahoo Finance). The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October. Q3 GDP grew 4.5%, near target, with no sign of financial contagion or tighter capital controls as of 4 Nov.
for_you: Weaker Chinese demand can weigh on commodity exporters and firms selling into China. No financial contagion is visible.
rubric_hit: Growth near target; no contagion or capital controls = Normal

sources.title: Yahoo Finance — China regulator tells banks to pause IPOs, FT reports
KuCoin News — Chinese regulators suspend IPOs to stabilise markets

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
